comparator.name: Business Administration
comparator.sourceNotes: This example shows the Business and Management specialization. It includes a 60 EC common first year, 60 EC of specialization courses in year two, and a 30 EC minor or exchange alongside 30 EC of courses and thesis work in year three.
components: Choose a 30 EC minor or approved study abroad.
Contemporary Theories in Business and Management
Legal and Ethical Aspects of Corporate Social Responsibility
Bachelor’s Thesis in Business and Management
Start after completing the 60 EC first year and 60 EC of profile-specific compulsory courses, with approval of the bachelor program.

core: Broad business administration across strategy, organisations, marketing, people, operations, accounting and finance
Organisational behaviour, culture, leadership and change
Marketing, consumer behaviour, business value creation and entrepreneurship
Operations, supply chains, technology and digital business
Sustainable and ethical business, human rights and corporate responsibility
Qualitative and quantitative business research and evidence-based decision-making
adjacent: Technology Management through digital transformation, data and operational technology
Accountancy and Controlling through accounting, finance, audit and analytical decision-making
questions: How should organisations adapt strategy, leadership and business models amid technological and social change?
How can data and research improve operational, managerial and financial decisions?
How can firms create value while meeting governance, sustainability, ethical and human-rights responsibilities?

alternatives.label: Business, Organizations and Management
alternatives.concept: Study how organizations develop products, serve customers and manage people. Combine strategy, marketing, accounting, leadership and international business with quantitative and qualitative research.
alternatives.labelReason: The label names the programme's own broad academic organising fields and does not borrow Groningen's specialisation title as a claim of equivalence.
progression: Business foundations and research methods precede marketing, law, negotiation and market research. Accounting and introductory economics support later financial and economic analysis.

alternatives.label: Technology, Data and Digital Business
alternatives.concept: Study how organizations use data and digital technology. Build skills in programming, databases, algorithms and machine learning, and use business and ethics courses to examine how digital systems change decisions.
alternatives.labelReason: The label states the actual UCR organising fields and avoids presenting the route as Groningen's formal Technology Management specialisation.
alternatives.distinctness: This plan differs from the broad plan by 9 courses in each direction and from the other focused plan by 6 courses.
progression: Python and mathematical methods precede algorithms and advanced machine learning. Introductory data science and statistics support later prediction and applied market research.

alternatives.label: Finance and Business Decisions
alternatives.concept: Study how companies and financial institutions make decisions. Combine accounting, finance and economics with econometrics, behavioral economics and market research.
alternatives.labelReason: The plan uses economics, financial analysis and quantitative evidence to study decisions by businesses and financial institutions.
alternatives.distinctness: This plan differs from the broad plan by 8 courses in each direction and from the other focused plan by 6 courses.
progression: Accounting and economics support later finance and behavioral economics. Research methods, probability and data analysis precede econometrics and market research.

candidates.label: Finance and Business Decisions
candidates.assessment: The available UCR curriculum supports finance and quantitative decisions. Accounting is present, while dedicated audit and management-control coursework are outside the plan.

routeSelection.basis: The generic degree has three profiles. Business and Management is the broadest general management profile. The other profiles focus on accountancy and controlling or technology management.

blocks: Groningen studies operations management. UCR’s product-design course contributes practical experience with prototyping and production scale.
Both study marketing planning, customer needs and the marketing mix.
Groningen extends management and organization theory in the final year.
Groningen has a dedicated management science course. UCR develops related quantitative techniques across several courses.
Groningen offers dedicated study of supply chain operations.
Groningen studies recruitment, motivation and job design. UCR examines workplace psychology and leadership.
Both study motivation, group behavior and leadership in organizations.
Groningen studies strategy at several organizational levels. UCR offers related work in negotiation and digital strategy.
Groningen studies management and organization theory in a dedicated course. UCR covers related behavior and strategy in separate courses.
Groningen studies organization and technology together. UCR explores the effects of AI and digital change in business.
Groningen connects organizational change and leadership. UCR addresses these through several management courses.
Groningen includes a dedicated consulting course.
Both use accounting and financial reports to understand business decisions.
Groningen covers financial management in a dedicated course. UCR develops related skills across accounting, corporate finance and financial markets.
Both use microeconomics to study firms, markets and decisions. UCR emphasizes behavior as well.
Groningen has a separate management accounting course.
Groningen offers dedicated management control coursework.
Both analyze quantitative evidence. UCR emphasizes econometric estimation and inference.
Both develop market research through data collection and analysis.
Groningen requires a 10 EC thesis. UCR shows optional independent research separately.
Both teach statistical analysis and inference. UCR also develops general research design.
Both develop qualitative research design, data collection and interpretation. UCR focuses on social research.
Groningen requires a separate business research design course.
Groningen includes an entrepreneurship lab. UCR teaches business foundations and product design.
Both examine how firms plan and carry out digital transformation.
Groningen studies legal and ethical aspects of corporate responsibility. UCR addresses related questions through international business and governance.
Groningen introduces management of digital businesses. UCR studies related questions in strategy and technology courses.
Both develop academic source use, argument and communication.
Groningen teaches business ethics and law together. UCR offers related work in governance and transnational business law.
Choose a minor or apply to study abroad.

selection.assessment: The closest programme covers Groningen's broad business-administration and Business and Management core. Two further formal specialisations are generator-backed and support coherent UCR responses: a technology, data and digital-business route and a finance, accounting and decision-analysis route. Pairwise differences are 60 EC, 67.5 EC and 45 EC; all exceed the 30-EC floor and reflect different academic organising logics. The maximum of three alternatives is reached.

notes.text: Groningen requires dedicated study in supply chains, operations, management accounting and management control, plus a thesis. The UCR plans offer related study in management, digital business and finance. The finance plan includes accounting and financial analysis, with further specialist study needed for auditing and management control.

audience.programmeDescription: This mainly Dutch-taught bachelor studies how organizations work, make decisions and respond to change.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The Groningen example follows Business and Management. The UCR plans emphasize general management, digital business or financial decisions.
